source_title: "Organ Bank" Mechanical Coin Bank (Cat and Dog)
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of an organ with a monkey, dog, and cat on top. To make a deposit, a coin is placed on the tray in the monkey's hand; cranking the lever will then cause the monkey to lower his arm and let the coin slip off tray and into the bank. While this is happening the dog and cat move counter clockwise and bells rings. Manufactured by the Kyser and Rex Company circa 1882. Title: "Organ Bank" Mechanical Coin Bank (Cat and Dog)

The Vollis Simpson Whirliigig Park on Goldsboro Street S. at Douglas Street S. in Wilson, North Carolina, opened on November 2, 2017 to document, conserve, and display the large whirlgigs from Simpson's property in Lucama, North Carolina. Wilson held its first annual Wilson Whirligig Festival in 2004. It was renamed in 2016 to the North Carolina Whirligig Festival, and is usually held the first full weekend of November. The North Carolina legislature named the whirligig the state's official folk art in June 2013.

Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a horse near a trough. To operate the bank, a coin is placed in the horse's mouth. Pulling a lever on the side of the bank causes the trough floor to open and lowers the horse's head, allowing the coin to fall through the trough into the bank. Manufactured by the Shepard Hardware Company circa 1885. Title: Trick Pony Mechanical Coin Bank

source_title: African American Caricature Mechanical Coin Bank
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a bust of an African American man wearing a red shirt and black tie. To operate the bank, a coin is placed in the figure's hand and a lever pressed causing the figure to roll his eyes as the hand deposits the coin in the figure's mouth. Manufactured by the Shepard Hardware Company circa 1883. Title: African American Caricature Mechanical Coin Bank

source_title: Monkey and Coconut Mechanical Coin Bank
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a monkey and a coconut. To make a deposit, a coin is placed in the monkey's right hand. Pushing a lever causes the monkey to drop the coin into the coconut. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1886. Title: Monkey and Coconut Mechanical Coin Bank

Cast iron bank in the shape of a bank building. "Home Bank" written above the front door. The door will move and a cashier will come out and take a coin. Coin slot on the back of the bank. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1872. Title: "Home Bank" Mechanical Coin Bank
